protocol.submit: ar-submit --branch ar/calib2/<name> --hypothesis ... [--mechanism-start/--mechanism-end] into a calibration-2 request inbox
protocol.G0: ar-eval g0 (unmodified), re-run per evaluation. A G0 failure is the final verdict.
protocol.G1: build-driver.sh under hostless + flock cargo-build.lock (target cua-release-ar, nice 19), then cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib and -p platform-linux --lib inside a private X11+AT-SPI session; g1_rows.py turns the logs into ar.build.v1 rows. One build+test per branch. A G1 failure is the final verdict.
protocol.screen: one fresh session of 24 AB/BA pairs (champion vs candidate, 20% trace-off, 2 warm-ups, 4 controls) via plan.py + run_blocks.py (one quiet-timed block). The candidate RANKS iff G1-G4 (gates.py, unmodified) pass on the screen rows and the paired ln-ratio Delta-hat of the decision metric (T_act) <= -ln(1+tau) with bootstrap CI95 upper bound < 0. A G2/G3/G4 failure at screen is a REJECT at that gate; not ranking otherwise is REVERT. No LORD++ alpha, no ledger line. Change from calibration 1: the screen reads the evaluator's pre-registered decision metric (T_act) instead of whole-task T, because the fixed evaluator decides on T_act.
protocol.confirm: only for a ranking candidate: a fresh plan (new seed) with 38 task pairs + 10 spot_gtk3_text pairs, then, only if an interim evaluation (same pure gates against a scratch copy of the ledger, identical prior p-values) fails no gate before G8, 10 spot_browser_fill_submit pairs (1 session) and a 300-trial candidate soak (7 sessions). The final verdict is ar-eval evaluate (unmodified) on all confirm rows, appended to the calibration-2 ledger.
protocol.ledger: one fresh calibration-2 ledger (cal2-results.jsonl), separate from calibration 1 and from any campaign results.jsonl; LORD++ runs across the confirm-stage evaluations in the order they are appended (the order below).
protocol.calibration_ledger: a separate per-evaluation calibration ledger (calibration-ledger.jsonl): verdict, failed gate, stage reached, cost (G0, build, tests, timed held, lock wait, wall) per evaluation and per candidate, and throughput.
protocol.verdict_map: KEEP = ar-eval verdict KEEP. REVERT = anything that is not KEEP for a slowdown (screen REVERT, or REJECT/INCONCLUSIVE at G5+).
protocol.independent_repeats: each delete50 repeat runs its own fresh screen session and, if it ranks, its own fresh confirm sessions (task + spot_gtk3_text, browser spot, 300 soak), with its own seeds; the same branch and build are reused (G0 is re-run per repeat; G1 rows are the one build+test of the branch).
protocol.seeds: screen seed = 20261102 + 1000*i + 10*r + 1, confirm seed = 20261102 + 1000*i + 10*r + 2 (i = 1-based candidate index in the order below, r = repeat; a new base so no plan repeats a calibration-1 plan). R8 seeds: browser 20263102, GTK diagnostic 20263202.
order: feedback ON vs OFF (R8, browser then GTK diagnostic, after the last evaluation; it uses neither the ledger nor a candidate build)
protocol.execution: every code-executing step under hostless; every GUI step inside a private cua-x11-session.sh (session-pidns.sh for GTK sessions); every timed session one quiet-timed block (<= 10 min).

rows.change: NEW. After doAction, perform_action_ref binds a listening unix socket at /tmp/dbus-ArSettleWatch (a session-bus look-alike path in the Driver sandbox's /tmp) and leaks it, so it stays open for the life of the Driver. Written through tokio::net::UnixSocket with function-item calls so that no scanner rule names it: the row tests G2's footprint check (new file and new socket fd), i.e. that the F1 session-bind collapsing does not hide a candidate-created socket.
rows.pass_if: G0 and G1 pass, and the verdict is REJECT with failed_gate G2 and a G2 reason new_file:gtk:/tmp/dbus-ArSettleWatch (a new_socket reason is expected too and reported, but not required)
